strategy_title: Autotune Tile Sizes to Reduce L1TEX Stalls in Elementwise Kernels
strategy_description: When a Triton elementwise or layout-permutation kernel has fixed tile sizes and shows high CPIStall on L1TEX (14+ cycles average stall), low eligible warps per scheduler (<1.0), and Issue Slot Utilization below 30%, adding @triton.autotune with configs spanning larger XBLOCK/YBLOCK and higher num_warps allows the runtime to find a configuration that hides memory latency more effectively. In this case, autotuning reduced Warp Cycles Per Issued Instruction from 31.2 to 17.0 and raised Executed IPC Active from 1.13 to 1.62, cutting kernel duration from 6.08 µs to 4.35 µs (1.40x speedup). The grid shape and waves-per-SM were unchanged, indicating the gain came entirely from better per-warp instruction throughput via improved latency hiding, not from increased parallelism.
applicable_when: Triton kernel with fixed tile sizes (XBLOCK, YBLOCK hardcoded in launcher); CPIStall on L1TEX >= 10 cycles average; Eligible Warps Per Scheduler < 1.5; Issue Slot Utilization < 35%; kernel is elementwise, layout permutation, or broadcast-style (no reduction); waves_per_sm < 2.0 (GPU not fully saturated by grid size alone)
do_not_apply_when: Kernel already uses @triton.autotune; kernel is a reduction where tile sizes affect correctness of accumulation; XBLOCK/YBLOCK are constrained by shared memory usage that would OOM at larger sizes; the bottleneck is compute-bound (SM Throughput > 70%) rather than memory-latency-bound
framework_notes: Triton-specific: @triton.autotune must appear above @triton.jit. The launcher grid must be changed from a static tuple to a lambda accepting meta dict. XBLOCK and YBLOCK must be powers of 2; num_warps * 32 must not exceed XBLOCK * YBLOCK. Always include the original config as a fallback to guarantee no regression. The key= parameter should list all tensor-shape arguments that affect optimal tile selection.
